newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end with modest gains, NAB lends support.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end with modest gains, NAB lends support.

text.p: The Australian share market finished modestly firmer on Thursday as investors mostly ignored a strong gain on Wall Street on Wednesday and focused buying attention on a handful of blue chip issues.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 6.8 points firmer at 2,413.2, after reaching an intra-day high of 2,419.7.
The June share price index ended up 11 points at 2,413 and at a 0.2 point discount to the underlying index.
Market heavyweights The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) were the most active issues with NAB stock underpinning the market's rise.

NAB shares closed 17 cents higher at A$16.28 (US$12.54). The stock was aided by the bank's current share buyback programme as well as speculation it could become a takeover target for a large foreign bank after last week's release of the Wallis report into Australia's financial system.
"There were a couple of stand out stocks apart from NAB. There was a lot of buying interest in Amcor and North," a dealer from a Sydney-based brokerage said.
Paper and packaging group Amcor, which closed 22 cents higher at A$8.23, attracted attention when it announced details of a re-organisation plan aimed at cutting costs and restoring profitability.
In contrast, oil and gas company Woodside Petroleum Ltd fell 32 cents to A$9.55 and other energy groups also lost ground after the price of oil fell sharply on offshore markets on Wednesday.

Shares in Anglo-Australian drug research and diagnostic group Cortecs International Ltd jumped on low volume, the stock nearly matching its London scrip which climbed 19 percent on Wednesday following a positive broker report.
The report said that Cortecs stock could double in price if the company announced a positive trial of a new drug to treat the bone-wasting disease, osteoporosis.
